strategy.summary: Reproduce numpy gh-31608/PR#31611: converting a NaT-like object whose year/month/day are float NaN to datetime64 raises TypeError on the buggy commit bee0b3f00c6e and should yield NaT after the fix. The project's added test test_datetime_nat_like_object_conversion in numpy/_core/tests/test_datetime.py must fail on buggy and pass on fixed.

system_packages: a C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang) and a BLAS-free NumPy build; ninja and meson-python build backend as used by the repo
build_commands: git apply the reproducing test diff onto numpy/_core/tests/test_datetime.py
pip install -r requirements/build_requirements.txt (or the repo's build requirements)
python -m pip install --no-build-isolation -e . (editable meson build of numpy at the buggy commit)
for the fixed revision: git checkout the PR#31611 merge/fix commit, rebuild the same way, then rerun the test
pinned_because: pytest: documented in README.md as required for running the test suite, no version pin evidenced, so latest compatible pytest is used
hypothesis, meson, cython: documented optional test dependencies, not exercised by this test, installed only if the build requires them

pandas and matplotlib: NOT documented and no era constraint; pandas is needed only for the issue#31608 reproducer, not for the project test, which uses a duck-typed NaTLike class. Unpinned by choice; the strategy does not depend on them for the transition

strategy.success_criterion: On buggy commit bee0b3f00c6e the test fails with TypeError ("'float' object cannot be interpreted as an integer") raised from np.asarray(NaTLike(), dtype=object).astype('datetime64[ns]') at the first assertion block. On the fixed revision (PR#31611) the test passes: the explicit-unit array is M8[ns] and np.isnat is True, np.datetime64(NaTLike(), 'ns') is NaT, and the unitless astype('datetime64') emits the DeprecationWarning matching "The 'generic' unit for NumPy datetime is deprecated" and yields a NaT array.
strategy.numerical_probe: np.isnat(np.asarray(NaTLike(), dtype=object).astype('datetime64[ns]')) should be True; on buggy it raises before reaching the check.

input_output_examples.buggy_output: TypeError: 'float' object cannot be interpreted as an integer

risks: The fix path is a datetime conversion, not a BLAS/threading path; MKL and Intel OpenMP from the reporter's runtime are incidental and should not be reproduced. Do not depend on them.

The unitless case emits a DeprecationWarning; if pytest is configured with filterwarnings=error the test's own pytest.warns still catches it, but any other warning escalation will fail. Keep default warning filters.

The test uses duck-typed NaN attributes, not a real pandas NaT. Real pandas NaT behaviour is described only in the PR text, so a pandas-based reproduction is not what the transition is decided by; the project test is authoritative.
Building numpy from source at the buggy and fixed commits requires a working compiler and meson toolchain; if the build environment cannot compile, the transition cannot be observed.
The era/dependency constraints for pandas, matplotlib, pytest, meson, cython, hypothesis are all unbounded with no documented constraint; the choices above are unverified defaults.
Architecture and sanitiser dependence is not evidenced in the context; the defect is expected to appear on any platform with the same CPython 3.12 object protocol, so no special platform is assumed.
The test command selects by -k name; verify the test class name (TestDateTime) matches the enclosing class in the file before relying on the nodeid form.

oracle.reference_source: PR#31611 test assertions: np.isnat checks and DeprecationWarning match string
oracle.why: NaT is checked via np.isnat, a boolean predicate, so no numeric tolerance applies.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On bee0b3f00c6e the first conversion np.asarray(NaTLike(), dtype=object).astype('datetime64[ns]') raises TypeError because year is float NaN and PyLong_AsLong rejects it, so the test errors before any assertion.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fix, convert_pyobject_to_datetime detects year == NPY_DATETIME_NAT and yields NaT with base NPY_FR_GENERIC, so np.isnat holds and the warning check is satisfied.
